entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
This petition is directed against an order passed by the Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority rejecting the petitioner's objection to the notice issued under section 10 of the U.P.
Industrial Area Development Act, 1976.

The order impugned records that plot no. 178, area 1.6957 hectares has already been subjected to acquisition proceedings under the Land Acquisition Act,
1894, out of which possession has already been taken over 1.4957-hectare land and an 80-meter road is proposed on such plot, which is withheld on account of petitioner unauthorizedly continuing in possession and raising constructions over it.

entities.text: Shyam Lal vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The order is assailed primarily on the ground that the State authorities have found various constructions over the acquired land.
A proposal was allegedly made to exempt certain land from the acquisition proceeding.

It is also submitted that since the constructions are old constructions,
therefore, the authorities cannot be permitted to initiate action for the demolition of such structures.

Learned counsel for the respondents, on the other hand, points out that acquisition proceedings have attained finality as no notification has been issued under section 48 of the Act of 1894 withdrawing any part of the acquired land from the acquisition proceedings and, therefore, the petitioner at best can claim compensation in accordance with the law.

It is also submitted that they have accepted the compensation amount, and the Authority is also prepared to consider their claim for allotment of land in lieu of acquisition under its lease back policy but on such pretext the petitioner cannot be permitted to continue in possession over acquired land.

From the facts brought on record, it is apparent that plot in question i.e. plot no. 178 situated in village Sirsa, Pargana Dankaur, Tehsil Sadar, District Gautam Buddh Nagar is a part of the notified industrial area of Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority by virtue of the provisions contained under the Act of 1976, and no development on such notified area can be made except on appropriate permission granted by the Authority under its building regulation of 2010.

Moreover the entire area of plot no. 178 is 1.6957, which had already been acquired pursuant to notification issued under section 4/17 of the Land Acquisition Act dated 12th March, 2008 and a declaration issued under section 6/17 dated 11.07.2008.
An award has also been passed, being award no. 95 of 2007, and compensation has also been paid to the petitioner.
According to the petitioner, the compensation received is only in respect of the one hectare land and not in respect of the remaining land.

There is nothing on record to show that any notification has been issued under section 48 of the Land Acquisition Act 1894 withdrawing any part of the acquired land of plot no. 178 from acquisition proceedings, and, therefore, the petitioner, at best, can come up with a claim for payment of compensation in respect of the balance land, if the compensation is not received, so far.
While doing so, the petitioner would also be entitled to compensation for structures standing on such acquired land in terms of the award.

However, as we find that the area is part of the notified area of the Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority and the entire plot has been subjected to compulsory acquisition under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, it would not be open for the petitioner to resist the action of the authorities in proceedings with developmental activity on the acquired land.
No infirmity is, therefore, pointed out in the order impugned, which may warrant any interference by this Court.
The writ petition stands dismissed.
Dismissal of this petition will not prejudice the petitioner's right to receive compensation in respect of any land for which compensation has not been received.

Similarly, the petitioner's claim for allotment of land under the lease back policy would also be adverted to within two months from the date of presentation of a copy of this order, if such claim is still pending.
